title: Insider Risk, eDiscovery and Audit

header.html: Describe the insider risk management solution; Describe communication compliance; Describe information barriers; Describe the eDiscovery solutions; Describe the Audit solutions
the official SC-900 study guide, skills measured as of October 21, 2026

html:
1Four jobs, four tools

Tool Job in one line Typical question
Insider Risk Management Detect risky actions by people inside the organization Is someone taking data before leaving?
Communication Compliance Detect inappropriate or policy-breaking messages Are messages offensive or leaking data?
Information barriers Block communication between groups to avoid conflicts of interest Should these two teams be able to chat?
eDiscovery Find, hold and export content for legal cases Which emails relate to this lawsuit?
Audit Record activities and let you search them Who did what, and when?

2Insider Risk Management

Helps detect, investigate and act on risky activities by users such as data theft, data leaks, security policy violations and sabotage, while protecting privacy.

Feature Meaning
Policies from templates For example data theft by departing users, data leaks, risky AI usage [Verify live]
Indicators and risk scores Signals from Microsoft 365 activity, risk levels for users
Alerts and cases Investigate and take action
Pseudonymization Usernames are anonymized by default to protect privacy
Triggers Events such as an HR resignation start closer monitoring
Exam tip

. "An employee about to leave downloads many files" = Insider Risk Management. It watches user behavior, not external attackers.

3Communication Compliance

Detects inappropriate content or regulatory violations in email, Teams, Viva Engage and other channels: harassment, threats, sharing sensitive information, and conflicts of interest. Reviewers can investigate and remediate messages. Policies use sensitive info types, keywords and trainable classifiers.

4Information barriers

Information barriers restrict communication and collaboration between defined groups to avoid conflicts of interest or meet legal separation (for example, between investment bankers and analysts in finance, or between teams working for competing clients). They apply to Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive and more. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. Information barriers = prevent two groups from talking or sharing (conflict of interest). Communication compliance = review the messages that were sent.

5eDiscovery

eDiscovery is the process of identifying and delivering electronic information used as evidence in legal, regulatory or internal investigations.

Tier Highlights
Content Search Search mailboxes, sites and Teams; basic
eDiscovery (Standard) Cases, holds to preserve content, search, export
eDiscovery (Premium) Adds custodians, review sets, analytics, predictive coding and advanced workflows

Microsoft retired the classic eDiscovery experiences on August 31, 2025; today you work in the new eDiscovery experience in the Microsoft Purview portal, and the Standard and Premium names describe the feature sets and licensing. [Verify live]

Key steps: create a case → place a legal hold → search → review → export. A hold stops people from deleting relevant content.

Exam tip

. Hold = preserve content for a case. Standard = cases, holds, search, export. Premium = custodians, review sets, analytics. [Verify live]

6Audit

Microsoft Purview Audit records user and admin activities across Microsoft 365 so you can search them for investigations, security and compliance.

Tier Highlights
Audit (Standard) Search the audit log, 180 days retention by default [Verify live]
Audit (Premium) Longer retention (up to 1 year, 10 years with add-on), audit retention policies, high-value events such as mail items accessed, higher bandwidth access via API

Examples of events: file opened, mailbox login, role change, label change.

Exam tip

. Audit = a searchable log of who did what. Premium = longer retention and more events. It helps investigations, and feeds Insider Risk Management and others.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors wants to spot employees who download unusual amounts of data before leaving the company. Which solution fits?

  • AAzure DDoS Protection
  • BConditional Access
  • CSafe Links
  • DInsider Risk Management
Show the answer

Answer: D. Insider Risk Management detects risky user actions such as data theft by departing users.

S2Two teams working for competing clients must not communicate or share files. Which feature fits?

  • AInformation barriers
  • BCommunication compliance
  • CSmart lockout
  • DContent explorer
Show the answer

Answer: A. Information barriers prevent communication between defined groups.

S3Legal asks IT to preserve and export emails relevant to a lawsuit. Which solution fits?

  • ASecure score
  • BeDiscovery
  • CAzure Firewall
  • DEntra Connect
Show the answer

Answer: B. eDiscovery finds, holds and exports content for legal matters.

S4An administrator needs to find who deleted a file last week. Which solution helps?

  • AMicrosoft Purview Audit
  • BAzure Bastion
  • CDefender for Cloud
  • DKey Vault
Show the answer

Answer: A. Audit records user and admin activities and supports searching.

S5Which solution detects harassing language in Teams messages?

  • AInformation barriers
  • BInsider Risk Management data theft policy
  • CCommunication Compliance
  • DeDiscovery hold
Show the answer

Answer: C. Communication Compliance reviews messages for inappropriate content.

S6What does a hold in eDiscovery do?

  • AEncrypts the content with a customer-managed key
  • BSends it to Sentinel for threat analysis later
  • CMoves it to a record in the file plan folder
  • DPreserves content so it cannot be deleted
Show the answer

Answer: D. A hold preserves relevant content for the case.

7.2 Recall questions

R1What does Insider Risk Management protect against?

Show the answer

Risky actions by people inside the organization, such as data theft and leaks.

R2What do information barriers prevent?

Show the answer

Communication between defined groups to avoid conflicts of interest.

R3Name the eDiscovery tiers.

Show the answer

Content Search, eDiscovery (Standard) and eDiscovery (Premium).

R4What are the basic eDiscovery steps?

Show the answer

Case, hold, search, review, export.

R5What does Audit record?

Show the answer

User and admin activities in Microsoft 365.

R6What does Audit Premium add?

Show the answer

Longer retention and more high-value events.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Insider Risk risky user actions; templates; risk scores; pseudonymized by default
Communication Compliance review messages for harassment, leaks, violations
Information barriers block groups from communicating (conflict of interest)
eDiscovery case, hold, search, review, export; Standard vs Premium
Audit searchable log of activities; Premium longer retention
